Constance S4 [Next, it was declared and decided that three persons should be chosen from each nation who know both the reasons of those wishing to depart and the punishments that ought to be inflicted on those departing without permission. [20 ]]

Constance S5 [Decrees of the council, concerning its authority and integrity, which had been abbreviated by cardinal Zabarella at the preceding session, against the wishes of the nations, and which are now restored, repeated and confirmed by a public decree]

Constance S6 [At this session there were, among other minor deliberations, decrees about admitting the office of proctor in the matter of pope John XXIII’s renunciation of the papacy and about the citing of Jerome of Prague.]
Constance S7 [At this session it was decreed that pope John should be publicly summoned and that the summons of Jerome of Prague, now charged with contumacy, should be repeated.]

Constance S8 [Condemnation of 260 other articles of Wyclif] [25]
Constance S8 [The council pronounces John Wyclif a heretic, condemns his memory and orders his bones to be exhumed]
Constance S9 [Pope John is publicly summoned for the second time and an inquiry against him is decreed.]
Constance S10 [John XXIII is summoned for the third time, he is accused of contumacy and is suspended from the papacy.]
Constance S11 [Pope John XXIII is publicly charged and forty-four articles against him are produced.]
Constance S12 [Decree stating that the process for electing a pope, if the see happens to be vacant, may not begin without the council’s express consent [27 ]]
Constance S12 [Sentence deposing pope John XXIII]
Constance S12 [Decree to the effect that none of the three contenders for the papacy may be re-elected as pope]

Constance S13 [That no priest, under pain of excommunication, may communicate the people under the forms of both bread and wine]
Constance S14 [Uniting of the followers of pope Gregory XII and of the former pope John XXIII, now that both men have abdicated]

Constance S14 [Decree stating that the election of the Roman pontiff is to be made in the manner and form to be laid down by the sacred council, and that the council shall not be dissolved until the election of the next Roman pontiff has been made]
Constance S14 [The council approves Gregory XII’s resignation]

Constance S16 [Deliberation about the council’s legates due to depart with the emperor Sigismund for Spain; minor deliberations about the conduct of the council’s business.]
Constance S17 [The emperor’s imminent departure from the council is treated of; the council offers prayers for his success.]

Constance S18 [Decrees about various matters to be decided by the council: power is given to judges to make decisions, and for pairs of them to hear cases; that bulls of the council are to be obeyed; that forgers of conciliar bulls are to be punished in the same way as forgers of apostolic letters; that letters are to be despatched regarding the graces granted by the former pope John, except expectative and exceptional graces; ambassadors to Italy are appointed .]

Constance S19 [Jerome of Prague finally abjures his faith publicly and solemnly. There is promulgated at this session an Ordinance between the friars Minor of the strict observance and others of the common life , to put an end to the discords which have arisen in certain provinces; another Ordinance by which cases of heresy are committed to certain judges . It is also decreed that, notwithstanding safe conducts of emperors and kings and others, a competent judge can inquire into heresy; that the lord vice-chancellor shall expedite the Caroline constitution [38 ] under a bull of the council; that those with benefices who are attending the council shall receive the fruits of their benefices in their absence, that the letters regarding provisions to patriarchal, metropolitan and other churches, which were granted by the former pope John before his suspension, shall be despatched .]
Constance S20 [A warning is decreed against the duke of Austria, on behalf of the bishop of Trent.]
Constance S21 [Sentence condemning Jerome of Prague]

Constance S22 [The treaty of Narbonne, between the king of Aragon, the emperor and the envoys of the council, is confirmed [39 ] : the king of Aragon withdraws obedience from Benedict XIII and recognises the council of Constance through his envoys.]
Constance S23 [Beginning of the process against Peter de Luna, called Benedict XIII in his obedience.]
Constance S24 [A citation against Peter de Luna, called Benedict XIII in his obedience, is decreed.]
Constance S27 [The dispute between Frederick, duke of Austria, and the bishop of Trent is discussed: a report is made on the carrying out of the warning decreed in session 20.]
Constance S28 [The Trent dispute is concluded: Frederick, duke of Austria, is condemned.]
Constance S29 [Peter de Luna is accused of contumacy.]
Constance S30 [The process against Peter de Luna continues.]
Constance S31 [A warning is decreed against Philip, count of Vertus, at the request of the bishop of Asti. Other minor deliberations take place.]
Constance S32 [Peter de Luna is again accused of contumacy and an inquiry about him is established.]
Constance S33 [The process against Peter de Luna, who is deemed contumacious, continues.]
Constance S34 [Everything is made ready for the condemnation of Peter de Luna.]
Constance S35 [The envoys of the king of Castile are united with the council in accordance with the terms of the treaty of Narbonne.]
Constance S36 [It is decreed that Peter de Luna is to be cited to hear the council’s sentence.]
Constance S37 [Definitive sentence whereby Peter de Luna, pope Benedict XIII, is divested of the papacy and deprived of the faith.]

Constance S38 [Decree about the right to vote of the deputies of the kings of Castile and Aragon, concerning which agreement had not been reached among the said deputies in the previous session; decrees about other lesser matters.]

Constance S41 [Everything is prepared for the start of the conclave to elect a pope. On 11 November cardinal Oddo Colonna is elected pontiff as Martin V.]

Constance S42 [In this session a bull of Martin V was approved regarding Baldassare Cossa, formerly pope, who was earlier deprived of his see and imprisoned by the council but who is now to be set free]

Lateran V S1 [The bull convoking the council, Sacrosancta Romanae Ecclesiae, and the bulls postponing it, Inscrutabilis and Romanus pontifex, are read out1{Msi 32, 681-690}. Masses are ordered to be celebrated, and prayers to be offered, to beg God’s assistance; various arrangements are to be observed in the council and decrees are set out; advocates, procurators, notaries, guards and vote-scrutineers are chosen; assigners of places, and the location of places in their due order, are established.]
